items.title: Think Nvidia Stock Is a Bargain? 6 Reasons the Face of the AI Build-Out Can Plunge Another 50% Following Jensen Huang's Resignation.
items.summary: Following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal misconduct allegations, Nvidia stock has fallen 32% from its peak. The article outlines six major risks that could drive the stock down another 50%: loss of company identity without Huang, potential slowdown in data center expansion due to Democratic governors, aggressive Fed rate hikes driven by AI-related inflation, warning signs in bond markets for hyperscalers, historical precedent of AI bubble-bursting events, and unsustainable premium valuations similar to the dot-com era.

items.title: Opinion: Buy This Growth Stock to Beat the S&P 500 in 2027
items.summary: DigitalOcean, an AI cloud services provider, has surged 65% in 2026 compared to the S&P 500's 10% return. The company is experiencing explosive demand for its AI Native Cloud platform, with AI customer revenue growing 288% and token volume increasing tenfold in Q3 2026. Management forecasts over 60% revenue growth for 2027, and the stock's valuation has become more attractive following a recent correction, positioning it to potentially outperform the broader market again next year.

items.title: Why Advanced Micro Devices Stock Surged This Week
items.summary: AMD stock rallied 19% this week driven by strong AI infrastructure spending signals and a major deal with Google Cloud to supply 5th Gen EPYC server processors. CoreWeave's raised capital expenditure guidance to $37-39 billion and Google Cloud's selection of AMD processors for confidential computing systems reinforced investor confidence in sustained data center demand. However, AMD's elevated P/E ratio of 117.6 leaves little room for error, with future performance dependent on maintaining hyperscaler capital spending momentum.

items.title: ROSEN, A RANKED AND LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages Everest Group, Ltd. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - EG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased Everest Group common stock between February 8, 2024 and October 27, 2025 of an important December 28, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in an ongoing securities class action. The lawsuit alleges that Everest made materially false statements regarding casualty risk exposure, inadequate pricing, insufficient reserves, and overstated earnings.

items.title: Jamie Dimon Just Said 5 Words Blocking Outside AI Agents From JPMorgan Accounts: "You Don't Want Rogue Agents." Here's Why That Security Stance Matters for JPM and Its Tech Rivals.
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned against allowing third-party AI agents like Meta's Muse to access customer accounts, citing security and regulatory risks including potential unauthorized transactions and compliance violations. United Airlines similarly announced restrictions on third-party AI agents for bookings, signaling that heavily regulated industries are taking a cautious stance on agentic AI integration.

items.title: Sundar Pichai Reported Alphabet's Cloud Revenue Grew 103% Last Quarter While the Gemini App Reached 1 Billion Monthly Users. Is Google Cloud Becoming a Bigger Growth Driver Than Search?
items.summary: Alphabet reported Google Cloud revenue grew 103% year-over-year to $30.7 billion in Q3, while the Gemini App reached 1 billion monthly users. However, Google Search growth slowed to 12% from 17% in Q2, raising concerns about AI's impact on search monetization. Cloud is emerging as Alphabet's primary growth engine with a $561 billion customer backlog, but the stock fell 28% from its peak amid worries about search's long-term viability and massive capital spending pressures.

items.title: רוזן, יועץ משפטי מוביל למשקיעים, מעודד את משקיעי Duolingo, Inc להשיג ייעוץ משפטי לפני המועד האחרון החשוב בתביעה ייצוגית בניירות ערך – DUOL
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is urging Duolingo, Inc. (DUOL) shareholders who purchased shares between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 to seek legal counsel before the December 7, 2026 deadline for a securities class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that Duolingo made false statements regarding user growth metrics by intentionally creating obstacles for users, including increased ads and paywall attempts, while knowing this would harm retention. The complaint also claims the company used low-quality AI-generated content that damaged user experience and financial performance.

items.title: ROSEN, A HIGHLY RECOGNIZED LAW FIRM, Encourages The Ensign Group, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - ENSG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased securities of The Ensign Group, Inc. between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026 about an important December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in a securities class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that Ensign made false statements regarding its business practices, including systematic neglect of elderly residents, fraudulent Medicaid/Medicare claims, falsification of nursing assistant hours, and illegal licensing schemes.

items.title: GlobalFoundries: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: GlobalFoundries reported record gross margins of 31.4% in Q3 2026, driven by a strategic shift away from lower-margin mobile devices toward high-growth optical networking and automotive silicon. The company expects silicon photonics revenue to hit $1 billion annualized run rate by end of 2027 (one year ahead of schedule) and plans to triple capacity in this segment. Notably, GFS is funding expansion through customer prepayments and government grants rather than heavy upfront capital spending, with planned 2027 net capex of approximately $4 billion. Over two-thirds of Q3 revenue now comes from non-mobile applications, demonstrating successful diversification.

items.title: INTC INVESTOR ALERT: Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP Files Class Action Lawsuit Against Intel Corporation and Announces Opportunity for Investors with Substantial Losses to Lead the Intel Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Intel Corporation alleging that executives made materially false and misleading statements about the company's business performance during July-October 2026. The suit claims Intel failed to disclose a significant slowdown in PC market demand, excess inventory at partners, and substrate supply constraints that offset AI-related gains. Intel's stock fell nearly 30% after revealing Q3 2026 CCPG revenue declined 9% sequentially and providing weak Q4 guidance.

items.title: רוזן, משרד עורכי דין המוכר ברמה גלובלית, קורא למשקיעי NuScale Power Corporation להסתייע בייעוץ משפטי לקראת מועד אחרון חשוב במסגרת תביעה ייצוגית בניירות הערך – SMR
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a securities class action lawsuit against NuScale Power Corporation (NYSE: SMR) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 27, 2026 and September 10, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that NuScale made false and misleading statements regarding its competitive advantages, revenue generation capabilities from the RoPower project and TVA work, and financial prospects. Investors who purchased during the class period may be eligible for compensation. The deadline to petition to be lead plaintiff is January 11, 2027.

items.title: ROSEN, A GLOBALLY RECOGNIZED LAW FIRM, Encourages NuScale Power Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - SMR
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against NuScale Power Corporation on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 27, 2026 and September 10, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding NuScale's competitive advantages, revenue generation capabilities from the RoPower Project and TVA work, and commercial prospects. The deadline to serve as lead plaintiff is January 11, 2027.

items.title: Why Intel Stock Slumped Today
items.summary: Intel stock fell nearly 3% on Friday amid concerns about leadership changes at Nvidia. The decline reflects uncertainty about Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress replacing Jensen Huang, and potential impacts on Nvidia's $13 billion Intel shareholding and their collaborative x86 CPU development. Investors are cautious until the situation clarifies.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 13: CoreWeave Falls Over 6% on AI-Cloud Selling and Reported $4 Billion Loan Talks
items.summary: CoreWeave shares fell 6.13% on November 13, 2026, as investors weighed concerns about the company's $4 billion loan pursuits against its strong 168% revenue growth. The decline was triggered by uncertainty following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and worries about CoreWeave's escalating debt burden exceeding $40 billion. Despite impressive Q3 results and doubled 2026 revenue guidance, debt and leverage concerns remain central to investor sentiment.

items.title: NVDA CLASS ACTION UPDATE: Rosen Law Firm Expands Class Period to Include More NVIDIA Corporation Investors in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - NVDA
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has expanded a securities class action lawsuit against NVIDIA Corporation, now covering investors who purchased securities between December 19, 2024 and November 12, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that NVIDIA made false and misleading statements regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy connected to Megaspeed (a company suspected of helping China evade export controls), undisclosed affairs with subordinate employees, and the company's relationship with Megaspeed. The firm claims these omissions posed material risks to NVIDIA's reputation and business prospects.

items.title: Bullfrog AI Holdings Inc. (BFRG) Reports Q3 Loss, Lags Revenue Estimates
items.summary: Bullfrog AI Holdings Inc. (BFRG) reported a Q3 loss of $0.11 per share, missing consensus estimates of $0.09 loss by 22.22%. Revenue came in at $0.06 million, missing estimates by 71.1%. The stock has declined 37.4% year-to-date and received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, expected to perform in line with the market.

items.title: SpaceX Expects to Spend $35 Billion to $40 Billion This Quarter. Here's Who Sells the Power and Cooling.
items.summary: SpaceX plans to spend $35-40 billion in Q4 2026, primarily on Nvidia GPUs for its data centers. The company is building power generation and cooling infrastructure at Starbase, creating opportunities for suppliers like GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Trane, and Vertiv to benefit from the massive capital expenditure and broader data center market growth.

items.title: Applied Materials: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Applied Materials reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of $34.4 billion, growing 21% year-over-year, driven by AI infrastructure demand. The company plans to double systems output by 2028 and has achieved 14 consecutive quarters of gross margin expansion, positioning it to outgrow the broader wafer fab equipment market.

items.title: AMD or Intel: 1 Chip Stock Is the Clear Winner
items.summary: AMD emerges as the superior investment choice compared to Intel, demonstrating stronger financial results with 45% revenue growth versus Intel's 21%, higher gross margins (54% vs 40%), and faster data center segment growth (97% vs 78%). AMD's better execution in outsourced manufacturing, stronger positioning for agentic AI demand, and more reasonable valuation (30.7x forward earnings vs Intel's 34.4x) make it the clear winner.

items.title: Why Sandisk Stock Is Falling Today
items.summary: Sandisk stock fell 8.2% on November 13, 2026, as a broader sell-off in AI hardware stocks spread following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation due to personal scandals involving alleged affairs and national security concerns. Despite Sandisk reporting strong fiscal Q1 results with $11 billion in sales (up 378% year-over-year) and 85.1% gross margins, investors worry the memory shortage could reverse as supply catches up or AI innovations reduce demand for expensive memory.

items.title: AMAT Q4 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and 2027 Growth Outlook
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) projects wafer fab equipment spending to rise over 30% in 2027, driven by AI-related semiconductor demand. The company plans to double systems output by 2028 and expects Q1 FY2027 revenues of $11.1 billion with 58% year-over-year growth. Management identified advanced packaging, DRAM, and foundry-logic as key growth drivers, though supply-chain bottlenecks and cleanroom availability remain constraints.

items.title: JPMorgan Stock Slid After Reports That Senate Democrats Plan a New Investigation Into Jamie Dimon's Bank Over Its Jeffrey Epstein Relationship. Here's Why That Political Risk Could Weigh on JPM Shares.
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase's stock declined following reports that Senate Democrats plan to investigate the bank's historical ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Epstein banked at JPMorgan from 1998-2013, with the bank processing over $1 billion in transactions and generating $8 million in fees. A former executive exchanged over 1,200 emails with Epstein despite red flags. While the bank settled a 2023 class action lawsuit for $290 million with no admission of wrongdoing, new investigations could lead to additional fines, regulatory orders, increased compliance costs, or reputational damage, potentially weighing on the stock in the near term.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against NVIDIA Corporation alleging that company executives made false and misleading statements regarding relationships with a company suspected of helping China evade export controls. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased NVIDIA securities between October 9, 2025 and November 8, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of January 8, 2027.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: Coherent's Margin Expansion Steals the Spotlight in Q1 FY27
items.summary: Coherent Corp. (COHR) demonstrated notable profitability improvements in Q1 FY27, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding 184 basis points to 40.6% and operating margin increasing 368 basis points to 23.2%. Non-GAAP EPS surged 80% year-over-year to $2.09, driven by stronger operational execution and improved cost efficiency. The stock has gained 61% over the past year and currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: TE Connectivity: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: TE Connectivity reported strong Q4 2026 results with $2.6 billion in full-year sales growth. The company expects over $1 billion in new Digital Data Networks revenue in 2027 driven by AI data centers, sees $500 content opportunity per humanoid robot unit, and achieved 100% free cash flow conversion while expanding capital investments. A book-to-bill ratio of 1.14 and strong backlog position the company for double-digit top-line expansion in fiscal 2027.

items.title: Is Realty Income Stock a Smart Monthly Dividend Bet Heading Into 2027?
items.summary: Realty Income (O) offers an attractive 5.5% dividend yield with 137 consecutive dividend increases and strong portfolio fundamentals including 98.8% occupancy. However, persistent inflation, potential Fed rate hikes, refinancing pressures, and moderate rental growth could limit earnings expansion and valuation upside into 2027. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting investors maintain positions while monitoring dividend coverage and financing costs.

items.title: SoFi vs. Upstart: Which Fintech Stock is the Better Buy Right Now?
items.summary: SoFi Technologies and Upstart Holdings represent different fintech approaches. SoFi operates as a digital bank with deposits, loans, and diversified revenue streams, while Upstart focuses on AI-driven lending partnerships. SoFi shares fell 14.5% versus Upstart's 37.1% decline over three months. SoFi trades at 3.27X forward P/S (below its median) with stronger growth prospects, while Upstart at 1.12X P/S faces headwinds from worsening borrower conditions and reduced guidance.

items.title: ARM Stock Gains 4% Since Q2 Earnings: Is it a Buy or Hold Now?
items.summary: Arm Holdings reported Q2 fiscal 2027 revenues of $1.44 billion, beating consensus estimates, with strong licensing growth and upbeat Q3 guidance. The company targets up to $2 billion in cumulative AGI CPU revenues through fiscal 2028. However, weak quarterly cash flow (down 73% YoY), uneven royalty growth, and lower silicon margins (30-40% vs. traditional licensing margins) warrant caution. The stock maintains a Hold rating despite strong AI infrastructure tailwinds.

items.title: PLTR's Rule of 40 Hits 158%: Can This Momentum Continue?
items.summary: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) achieved a Rule of 40 score of 158% in Q3 2026, up from 81% in Q4 2024, driven by 96% year-over-year revenue growth and a 62% adjusted operating margin. U.S. commercial revenues surged 148% to $984 million while government revenues climbed 96%, supported by expanding AI Platform adoption. The company generated $1.22 billion in free cash flow with a 53% margin, though elevated investor expectations and valuation multiples present risks.

items.title: NU Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Credit Growth and Global Expansion
items.summary: Nu Holdings (NU) reported Q3 earnings of $0.22 per share with revenues of $5.82 billion, beating consensus estimates. The company's credit portfolio grew 33% to $41.6 billion with improved lending margins at 12.7%. NU raised its 2026 efficiency outlook to 19%-19.5% and is expanding operations in Mexico, Colombia, and the U.S., while maintaining disciplined credit growth and conservative underwriting standards.

items.title: Block's Square Expands Agentic Platform With Squaremates & New AI Tools
items.summary: Block, Inc.'s Square has launched Squaremates, an AI-powered agentic platform that automates complex business tasks for sellers including marketing, labor cost analysis, staffing optimization, and inventory management. The expansion includes new MCP and CLI tools enabling third-party AI integrations and custom applications. Square also introduced a voice-enabled kiosk and released over 180 features in 2026, with Q3 gross payment volume increasing 14% year-over-year to $76.4 billion.

items.title: You Can Do Better Than Tesla: 3 Industrial Stocks With More Upside
items.summary: The article argues that three industrial stocks—Caterpillar, Lockheed Martin, and GE Vernova—offer better investment opportunities than Tesla. These companies benefit from AI-driven electricity demand and defense spending, with record order backlogs stretching years into the future. Caterpillar's power generation revenue surged 75%, Lockheed Martin's backlog reached $292 billion, and GE Vernova's backlog hit $197 billion, while Tesla faces margin pressures and a softening EV market.

items.title: Innventure: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Innventure announced a strategic pivot focused on cost reduction and debt restructuring. The company cut parent staff by 62% (from 40 to 15 employees), suspended new development, and stopped funding its operating subsidiaries. Each subsidiary—including liquid-cooling business Accelsius, flexible-packaging developer AeroFlexx, and waste-conversion unit Refinity—must now secure external capital independently. Management hired RBC Capital Markets to evaluate all options including debt restructuring and potential asset monetization.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Lululemon Athletica Inc. (NASDAQ: LULU) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Lululemon Athletica (NASDAQ: LULU) alleging that the company failed to disclose deteriorating store traffic and demand due to negative media commentary and weak product launches. The complaint claims defendants made materially false statements about the company's financial guidance and business strength, particularly in North America and Mainland China. Investors who purchased LULU securities between March 18, 2026 and September 3, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of January 4, 2027.

items.title: Costco Hits All-Time High Amid $4 Billion Buyback, Special Dividend
items.summary: Costco declared a record $30 per share special dividend ($13.3 billion) while reauthorizing a $4 billion buyback program through 2030. The company's restrained buyback usage suggests management views shares as fairly valued rather than cheap. Investors should focus on December 10th earnings results, where consensus expects $4.87 per share (up 12% YoY), though headline comparable sales growth of 11.1% masks a more modest 7.3% when excluding gasoline and FX impacts.

items.title: AECOM Q4 Earnings Ahead: What Should Investors Expect?
items.summary: AECOM is expected to report Q4 fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 16 with adjusted EPS projected at $1.59 (up 16.9%) but revenues expected to decline 1.9%. The company benefits from strong infrastructure demand and a $27.81 billion backlog (up 12%), with AI adoption supporting efficiency. Recent construction sector peers showed mixed results: Martin Marietta reported strong earnings with record volumes, CRH missed expectations and cut guidance, while MasTec exceeded estimates with robust backlog.

items.title: VIAV's Q1 Beat and Q2 Outlook Highlight Data Center Momentum Ahead
items.summary: Viavi Solutions (VIAV) delivered robust fiscal Q1 2027 results with revenues surging 56.9% to $469.3 million and earnings jumping 213.3%, beating consensus estimates. The company projects Q2 revenues of $505-$515 million with continued strength from data-center demand, 1.6T optics, and semiconductor testing. Operating margins expanded significantly to 29%, supported by the Spirent acquisition and operating leverage.

items.title: RITM vs. BX: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of Rithm (RITM) and Blackstone Inc. (BX) reveals that Rithm offers superior value for investors. RITM has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 3.87 and PEG ratio of 0.55, earning a Value grade of B. BX has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 20.13 and PEG ratio of 1.51, receiving a Value grade of D. Based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook, RITM is positioned as the better value opportunity.

items.title: PNC Financial Gains 10% in the 6 Months: What's Ahead for Investors?
items.summary: PNC Financial shares gained 10% over six months, outperforming peers through balance-sheet expansion, branch growth plans, and strategic acquisitions. The company raised its 2026 loan growth outlook to 13.5% and plans 370+ branches by 2031. However, rising operating expenses and heavy commercial loan concentration pose risks. PNC trades at an attractive 10.9X forward P/E with a 3.46% dividend yield, but investors may want to wait for clarity on expense trends before entering.

items.title: SO Q3 Earnings Beat on Data Center Demand, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Southern Company reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.94, up 21.3% year-over-year and beating estimates, with revenues climbing 13% to $8.84 billion. The company benefited from strong electricity demand, particularly from data centers (up 59%), and signed 4 GW of additional large-load contracts, bringing total contracted demand to 21 GW. Southern raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $4.70 and expanded its capital investment plan to approximately $85 billion through 2030.

items.title: This Video Game Publisher Has a Huge Catalyst Looming
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) is positioned for significant growth with Grand Theft Auto VI launching on November 19th. The company's latest quarterly results showed weakness with declining revenue, but management reaffirmed strong FY27 guidance of $8.0-$8.2 billion (roughly 20% growth), with GTA 6 as the primary driver. The unprecedented preorder activity and the decade-long success of GTA 5 (230 million copies sold) suggest strong long-term revenue potential through both initial sales and recurring GTA Online monetization.

items.title: TSMC’s Terrific Growth Clearly Shows That the Chip Sell-Off Is Overdone. Here Are the Best Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist
items.summary: Despite a 17% decline in the semiconductor sector since early October, TSMC's October sales surged nearly 60% year-over-year, demonstrating that the chip sell-off is overdone. The company's accelerating growth is driven by robust AI infrastructure investments and agentic AI adoption. TSMC plans to increase capital expenditure to $60-64 billion in 2026, significantly benefiting equipment suppliers like ASML. Both TSMC and ASML are trading at attractive valuations and are well-positioned to capitalize on the AI-fueled chip boom.

items.title: Domino's Strong Order Trends vs. Weak Ticket Growth: What Lies Ahead?
items.summary: Domino's Pizza reported Q3 2026 U.S. same-store sales growth of 0.3%, driven by strong order count increases that offset declining average ticket sizes due to consumer spending pressures. The company is implementing value promotions and new products like The Domino to boost ticket growth, while expecting continued order momentum in Q4 but sales near the lower end of guidance. Domino's shares have outperformed the broader market, trading at a lower valuation than industry peers.

items.title: CBRS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on Strong Cloud Growth
items.summary: Cerebras Systems (CBRS) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 13 cents per share, beating estimates, with revenues surging 70% year-over-year to $230.87 million. Cloud revenues soared 272% to $144.91 million driven by AI inference demand and higher pricing. The company secured partnerships with Oracle and Microsoft, raised 2026 revenue guidance to $940-$960 million, and expects to triple revenues in 2027 with expanding data center capacity.

items.title: Cisco: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Cisco reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $18.5 billion, up 24% year-over-year, with AI infrastructure revenue projected to reach $9 billion in FY2027, more than double FY2026 levels. The company achieved operating leverage by reducing headcount while expanding revenue, expecting a 19% increase in revenue per employee. Management highlighted a multiyear networking super cycle driven by hyperscaler demand and enterprise modernization across data centers and campus networks.

items.title: Cisco's Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong Networking Aids Revenues
items.summary: Cisco Systems reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $1.40 per share, up 40% year-over-year, with revenues surging 24% to $18.52 billion. Networking revenues jumped 43%, driven by AI infrastructure growth and strong campus networking demand. The company raised its fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue guidance to $9 billion from $7.5 billion and increased full-year revenue outlook to $74.8-$75.8 billion, reflecting sustained customer demand and broad-based growth.

items.title: NBIS Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Expansion Plans and Funding
items.summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) reported strong Q3 2026 earnings with 571% year-over-year revenue growth to $980.8M, beating estimates. The company targets $12-13B in 2027 revenues with pretax breakeven expected in Q4 2027. Management plans $40-45B in capex for 2027, with 75-85% funded through customer prepayments and asset-backed financing. Despite facility deployment delays, the company sees improving contract economics with customer prepayments now exceeding 100% of new capacity capex.

items.title: Corteva Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Brazil Woes and Outlook Cut
items.summary: Corteva reported Q3 2026 earnings that missed expectations with adjusted EPS of 6 cents versus 9 cents consensus and revenues of $1.52 billion versus $1.77 billion expected. The company significantly reduced full-year EBITDA guidance to $1.1-$1.13 billion from $1.3 billion due to severe conditions in Brazil, including $250 million in excess channel inventory, pricing pressure, and a 31% decline in Latin American organic sales. Management is implementing cost reduction initiatives and expects recovery in 2027 supported by inventory normalization and new product growth.

items.title: Cisco Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Higher Outlook
items.summary: Cisco raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $74.8B-$75.8B with non-GAAP EPS of $5.47-$5.53, driven by accelerating hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand and broad-based networking momentum. The company increased its hyperscaler AI revenue target to $9B from $7.5B, with networking orders up 28% and product orders up 21%. However, gross margin declined 250 basis points to 65.6% due to higher hardware exposure and rising memory costs.

items.title: AMAT Q4 Earnings Beat on Record Semiconductor Systems Sales
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) reported Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings of $4.16 per share, up 92% year-over-year, with record revenues of $10.41 billion, up 53%. The company expects continued growth with Q1 FY27 revenue guidance of $11.1 billion and earnings of $4.35 per share, driven by robust demand for advanced chipmaking equipment and AI-related memory investments.

items.title: GridAI Technologies Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Pronghorn Resources, Establishing Major Wyoming Owned-Natural Gas and Multi-Gigawatt AI Power Infrastructure Platform Targeting Initial Power Delivery in 2027
items.summary: GridAI Technologies (Nasdaq: GRDX) announced a definitive agreement to acquire Pronghorn Resources, a Wyoming-based natural gas producer with ~100 MMcf/day production and 450+ miles of owned pipelines. The acquisition establishes a vertically integrated energy and AI infrastructure platform targeting 300 MW initial power delivery in 2027 to support hyperscale data center development. GridAI also acquired exclusive Wyoming rights for 1st American Nuclear Co.'s EAGL-1 240 MWe SMR platform.

items.title: Wells Fargo Eyes $50B NII in 2026: What's Fuelling the Optimism?
items.summary: Wells Fargo reaffirms its $50 billion net interest income (NII) target for 2026, with Q4 NII expected near $13 billion. The bank's NII grew 5.1% year-over-year to $36.93 billion in the first nine months of 2026, driven by expanding loan balances (up 11%), growing deposits (up 9%), and fixed-rate asset repricing. The removal of the asset cap and mid-single-digit growth projections for loans and deposits support the outlook.

items.title: Wall Street Divided on S&P 500: Which ETFs Could Benefit in 2027?
items.summary: Wall Street strategists are divided on the S&P 500's 2027 outlook. UBS forecasts the index reaching 8,900 (17.22% upside) driven by earnings growth, while Bank of America warns that crowded equity positioning, AI valuation risks, and potential outflows could limit gains. The divergence highlights key risks including elevated valuations, geopolitical uncertainty, and concentration in mega-cap tech stocks.

items.title: Home Depot Pre-Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy or Stay Cautious?
items.summary: Home Depot is expected to report Q3 fiscal 2026 results on November 17 with projected revenue growth of 3.3% to $42.7B and EPS growth of 3.5%. While the company benefits from strong Pro sales, digital expansion, and smaller home improvement projects, near-term challenges include weak housing turnover, margin pressures from tariffs and operating costs, and a premium valuation of 22.27X forward P/E.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway’s Greg Abel Bought Back a Record $9.6 Billion of Stock Last Quarter. Here’s Why That Pace Might Not Continue.

However, the pace is likely to slow significantly as Berkshire's stock price has climbed above key valuation thresholds. With the price-to-book ratio now at 1.6 (compared to Buffett's previous buyback threshold of 1.5), Abel is unlikely to continue aggressive repurchases unless the stock price pulls back, adhering to Buffett's principle that buybacks should only occur at discounts to intrinsic value.

items.summary: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as NVIDIA CEO due to personal scandals, investors are rotating toward competing semiconductor companies including AMD, Broadcom, and TSMC. The company's board investigation found no compromise of secrets or national security. Despite the scandal, the article argues Nvidia remains an attractive AI infrastructure leader trading at a forward P/E of 11x fiscal 2028 estimates, with strong competitive advantages in GPU technology and strategic partnerships.

Since 2017, STLD has repurchased $8.2 billion in shares and distributed $2.2 billion in dividends. The company maintains a low-cost operating model and disciplined capital allocation strategy while preserving investment-grade credit ratings.

items.title: Arista Networks: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Arista Networks reported Q3 2026 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5% year-over-year, driven by surging AI infrastructure demand. The company forecasts fiscal 2027 revenue of $18.5 billion with 38-40% growth. Key strengths include its unified operating system architecture that minimizes security vulnerabilities, expansion of open Ethernet standards for AI deployments (projected to exceed 10 gigawatts by 2027), and accelerating enterprise campus growth expected to reach $2 billion in 2027.

items.title: Everest Group, Ltd. Notice of December 28, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: A class action securities lawsuit has been filed against Everest Group, Ltd. for allegedly making false statements about insurance reserve adequacy. The company disclosed $478 million in unfavorable prior year reserve development and secured $1.2 billion in protection against further adverse development, causing the stock to fall 11.4% on October 28, 2025. Investors who purchased shares between February 8, 2024 and October 27, 2025 can join the lawsuit with a December 28, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. Notice of November 23, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC announced class action securities lawsuits against Honeywell Aerospace, Everest Group, and Millrose Properties for alleged securities fraud. Honeywell Aerospace is accused of failing to disclose supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, and a false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts. Investors who purchased shares during specified periods can seek lead plaintiff status before application deadlines.

items.title: The Ensign Group, Inc. Notice of December 7, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
items.summary: A class action securities lawsuit has been filed against The Ensign Group, Inc. for allegedly making materially false statements and failing to disclose systematic neglect of elderly residents in its facilities. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased Ensign securities between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026. Investors have until December 7, 2026 to request appointment as lead plaintiff.

items.title: Intel vs. SK Hynix: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy?
items.summary: SK Hynix is recommended as the better investment choice over Intel for the near term. SK Hynix benefits from surging AI memory demand with record revenue growth of 46.8% and a 44.2% net margin, while Intel faces execution risks in its foundry transition, weaker PC demand, and missed guidance expectations. SK Hynix trades at a significantly lower valuation multiple (3x forward P/E vs. Intel's 33.3x).

items.title: Amazon’s Cloud Computing Business Already Brings in More Revenue Than 476 Companies in the S&P 500. Here’s What It Would Take to Reach $1 Trillion.
items.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has reached $161.4 billion in trailing-12-month revenue, surpassing 476 S&P 500 companies. CEO Andy Jassy believes AWS could become a $1 trillion revenue business within 5-10 years. With accelerating revenue growth exceeding 40% expected in 2027-2028 and substantial capital expenditure investments in AI infrastructure, AWS appears positioned to achieve this ambitious target through sustained cloud adoption and improved returns on invested capital.

items.title: ALPHABET (GOOG) ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C Urgently Reminds Alphabet Inc. Investors to Contact the Firm Seeking Lead Plaintiff Role Before December 1st
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026. The complaint alleges that Alphabet made materially false and misleading statements by failing to disclose that the Gemini 3.5 Pro was delivering disappointing training results and would face significant launch delays. Investors have until December 1, 2026 to apply to be appointed as lead plaintiff.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Reminds Investors with Losses on their Investment in Alphabet Inc. of Class Action Lawsuit and Upcoming Deadlines – GOOG
items.summary: Pomerantz Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Alphabet Inc., alleging securities fraud related to misleading statements about the Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model launch. The company announced a June 2026 launch at its May I/O conference, but Bloomberg reported in July that Google was months behind schedule. The stock fell 4.4% on the news. Investors have until December 1, 2026, to join the class action.

items.title: CoreWeave Delivers Another Blowout Quarter. Is It Enough To Save the AI Trade?
items.summary: CoreWeave reported strong Q3 results with 168% revenue growth to $3.66B and improved operating margins, but concerns persist about its balance sheet. The company carries $47B in debt with interest expenses jumping to $846M per quarter and a free cash flow loss of $7.7B. While management pledged to avoid unsecured debt and expects $9B in customer prepayments in Q4, investors remain cautious given rising interest rates and the company's current ratio below 0.5.

items.title: NOVAGOLD Announces Expected Completion Date for Donlin Gold Acquisition, NYSE Listing and TSX Delisting
items.summary: NOVAGOLD has obtained shareholder approval to acquire Paulson's 40% stake in Donlin Gold, consolidating 100% ownership of the Tier One gold project in Alaska. The transaction is expected to close on December 1, 2026, with a new U.S. parent company, NovaGold Corporation, listing on NYSE under ticker 'NG' on December 2. NOVAGOLD shares will delist from NYSE American and TSX following completion.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 10: Trade Desk Jumps After Q3 Results Show Revenue Topped Estimates
items.summary: The Trade Desk (TTD) surged 3.28% to $15.42 after Q3 results beat revenue estimates at $736 million. The company announced a $731 million buyback authorization increase, bringing total repurchase capacity to $1 billion. While Q4 guidance won't show year-over-year growth, management signaled confidence in the turnaround. Trading volume reached 64.9 million shares, 189% above average. The broader market declined with S&P 500 down 0.38% and Nasdaq down 0.74%.

items.title: Kimbell Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Oil Upside and Drilling Growth
items.summary: Kimbell Royalty Partners (KRP) missed Q3 earnings and revenue estimates but maintained Q4 guidance, reporting record production of 27,565 Boe/d (up 7%) and 93 active rigs. The company expects stronger Q4 cash flow with 84% of oil production unhedged, completed $367M in acquisitions, and announced a $0.45 per unit distribution representing 75% of cash available for distribution.

items.title: ROSEN, THE FIRST FILING FIRM, Encourages The Ensign Group, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - ENSG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is urging investors who purchased securities of The Ensign Group, Inc. (ENSG) between February 10, 2022 and June 18, 2026 to secure legal counsel before the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline. The lawsuit alleges that Ensign made false statements regarding its business model, claiming the company systematically neglected elderly residents, defrauded Medicare and Medicaid, falsified nursing assistant hours, and engaged in illegal licensing schemes while understating litigation risks.

items.title: 3 AI Stocks to Buy Now That Midterms Are Over
items.summary: Following the midterm elections, concerns about the AI trade have eased, particularly in Texas where data center construction pipelines remain safe through 2027-2028. Three AI stocks are positioned to benefit: Penguin Solutions, which specializes in memory products for data centers with 68% YoY revenue growth; Sandisk, whose NAND flash memory chips are essential for AI infrastructure with 378% YoY revenue growth; and Alphabet, which is advancing AI through Gemini and Waymo while Google Cloud revenue more than doubled YoY.

items.title: Devon Energy Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Permian Focus and Buybacks
items.summary: Devon Energy reported Q3 adjusted earnings of $1.42 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.24, though revenues missed expectations. The company outlined a 2027 capital spending plan of $5.3B with 75% directed to Permian Basin development, increased merger synergies to $700M, and accelerated shareholder returns including over $1B in Q4 buybacks and $1.5B in debt reduction.

items.title: Top Stock Picks for Week of November 9, 2026
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) strengthens its semiconductor market position through strong AI infrastructure demand for EPYC server CPUs and Instinct accelerators, with earnings expected to grow 90.9% in the current quarter and 92.8% for the fiscal year. Moderna raises its 2026 revenue outlook following stronger-than-expected Q3 sales, with third-quarter revenues increasing 29% year-over-year, supported by increased COVID vaccine demand and international partnerships.

items.title: Reasons to Hold Veeva Systems Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Veeva Systems (VEEV) is well-positioned for growth driven by its diversified product portfolio, strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results, and accelerating Vault CRM adoption with over 180 customers live and 12 of top 20 biopharma commitments. However, market saturation in the life sciences CRM sector poses a headwind to future growth rates. The company raised its fiscal 2027 outlook and expects 35% growth over the next five years.

items.title: Can Home Depot Sustain Comparable Sales Growth Amid Uneven Demand?
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q2'26 comparable sales growth of 1.7% year-over-year, driven by professional customer demand and 11% digital sales growth across 13 of 16 departments. However, comparable transactions declined 1%, indicating ticket-driven rather than volume-led growth. The company reaffirmed flat to 2% comps guidance for FY26 as persistent housing affordability pressures and consumer uncertainty continue to constrain larger discretionary renovation projects.

items.title: ROSEN, GLOBAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Duolingo, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - DUOL
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. alleging that the company made materially false statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates. The lawsuit claims Duolingo deliberately added user friction through increased ads and subscription upsells while using AI-generated content that degraded product quality, negatively impacting user retention and financial performance. Investors who purchased Duolingo Class A common stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is December 7, 2026.

items.title: EFX Stock Rallies 13% in 6 Months: Here's What You Should Know
items.summary: Equifax (EFX) gained 12.9% over six months, outperforming industry expectations through diversified revenue growth across Workforce Solutions, U.S. Information Solutions, and International operations. The company doubled its AI-driven cost-savings target to $150M and raised 2026 margin expansion guidance to 100 bps. Government contract wins exceeding $550M annually support continued Workforce Solutions growth, with the company successfully navigating weak mortgage market conditions.

items.title: Franklin Templeton Lifts 2029 Targets: What's Driving Its Optimism?
items.summary: Franklin Templeton (BEN) raised its fiscal 2029 adjusted operating margin target to 35% from 30%, driven by aggressive expansion in private markets (targeting $150B fundraising), ETFs (targeting $200B AUM), and customized investment solutions. The company has already raised $66B in private markets since fiscal 2024 and achieved 73% year-over-year ETF AUM growth to $84.6B in fiscal 2026. Despite execution risks from market volatility and fee pressures, BEN's diversified capabilities position it for sustained long-term growth.

items.title: Lam Research's Gross Margin Hits 52.4%: Can it Climb Further?
items.summary: Lam Research achieved a record non-GAAP gross margin of 52.4% in Q1'27, driven by strong revenue growth of 22%, favorable customer mix, and 40% year-over-year growth in its Customer Support Business Group. The company expects a 52.5% gross margin in Q2, though customer-mix headwinds and supply constraints may limit further gains. Competitors Applied Materials and KLA also showed strong margin expansion, benefiting from AI-driven semiconductor equipment demand.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark Has Raised Its Dividend for 55 Straight Years. Here's How Much $10,000 Invested Pays Annually.
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark, a Dividend King with 55 consecutive years of dividend increases, offers investors a $10,000 stake generating approximately $471 annually in dividends with growth potential. The company recently completed its $49 billion acquisition of Kenvue, adding major brands like Listerine and Tylenol while targeting $1.9 billion in cost efficiencies over three years. Consumer staples stocks like KMB are gaining favor as alternatives to the vulnerable AI trade.

items.title: Can Comfort Systems' Mechanical Margins Offset Electrical Weakness?
items.summary: Comfort Systems USA (FIX) delivered strong Q3 2026 results with Mechanical revenues up 43% and Electrical revenues surging 85%. While Mechanical segment margins expanded 80 basis points to 25.1%, Electrical margins declined 190 basis points to 24.3%, primarily due to absence of prior-year discrete gains. Consolidated operating margin improved to 16.6%, and the company expects 2027 gross margins to remain strong. FIX stock has outperformed its industry and the S&P 500 YTD, trading at a forward P/E of 17.7 with upward earnings revisions.

items.title: VST Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Power Pricing, Revenues Rise Y/Y
items.summary: Vistra Corp. reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.23 per share, beating estimates by 9.86% with an 84.6% year-over-year increase. Revenues reached $6.35 billion, up 27.7% but slightly missing consensus estimates. The company raised 2026 guidance and initiated 2027 outlook, supported by higher energy prices, the Cogentrix acquisition, and strong retail performance. Peer utilities Everergy, FirstEnergy, and IDACORP also reported better-than-expected Q3 results.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: Embraer Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates, Revenues Beat, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Embraer (EMBJ) missed Q3 earnings expectations with 40 cents per ADS versus consensus of 87 cents, though revenues grew 17.2% to $2.35 billion. The company delivered 66 aircraft and achieved a record $35.7 billion backlog. EMBJ raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.4-$8.6 billion and increased free cash flow outlook to at least $700 million, earning a Zacks Rank #1 Strong Buy rating.

items.title: GEHC Expands Vscan Air AI Capabilities With Lung Guidance & AutoAS
items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies announced the addition of two AI-assisted features—Lung Guidance and AutoAS—to its Vscan Air handheld ultrasound system. Lung Guidance achieved a 95.2% success rate for diagnostic-quality lung exams among non-expert users, while AutoAS aids in aortic stenosis assessment. These additions expand GE HealthCare's point-of-care ultrasound capabilities and could drive adoption and recurring revenue through Innovation Packages.

items.title: Is Now the Right Time to Hold Labcorp Stock in Your Portfolio?
items.summary: Labcorp Holdings (LH) has surged 48.2% year-to-date, driven by expansion in specialty testing markets, AI and automation initiatives, and six consecutive quarters of margin expansion. However, currency headwinds, intense competition, and acquisition-related execution risks could limit future growth. The company maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a 5% earnings yield.

items.title: Watsco: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Watsco reported 7% sales growth to $2.22 billion in Q3 2026, driven by HVAC volume and pricing gains. The company is expanding into plumbing distribution, leveraging its debt-free balance sheet and proprietary software to increase contractor loyalty and market share. Management targets a 30% gross margin through operational efficiency and views strategic M&A as key to compounding market share over the next three to five years.

items.title: McDonald's vs Wendy's: What's the Better Fast-Food Stock to Buy Right Now?
items.summary: McDonald's and Wendy's represent two different investment approaches in fast food. McDonald's offers stability with steady 1.5% comparable sales growth, a 50-year dividend increase streak, and a 2.64% yield, making it ideal for risk-averse investors. Wendy's, down 60% over five years with declining same-store sales, is pursuing a turnaround strategy called 'Dave's Way' and trades at a lower valuation with a 5.90% yield, offering potential upside for high-risk investors despite recent dividend cuts.

items.title: TTD Q3 Earnings Call Focuses on Resetting Growth and Execution
items.summary: The Trade Desk reported Q3 2026 revenues of $736 million, down 0.5% year-over-year but beating consensus estimates. Despite the beat, management emphasized the turnaround remains incomplete. The company projects cautious Q4 guidance of at least $755 million in revenue with no expected seasonal uplift. TTD is implementing a 15% workforce reduction generating $44M in restructuring charges, targeting over $100M in gross savings for 2027 while investing in AI, measurement, and customer relationships. International growth remains strong, but large global advertisers face continued pressure.

items.title: MonetizeMore Launches AdSense Policy Grader to Help Publishers Prevent Google Ad Bans
items.summary: MonetizeMore announced the AdSense Policy Grader (APG), an AI-powered audit tool that checks publisher websites against Google's policies. The tool offers a free 40-point check report and a paid $19.99 comprehensive 79-check report, helping publishers identify and fix compliance issues before they result in revenue loss or account termination. According to Google's 2025 report, over 480 million publisher pages had ads blocked or restricted in 2025.

items.title: TTWO Q2 Earnings Call Highlights GTA VI Outlook and Booking Trends
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) reported Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings of $1.00 per share, beating estimates by 11.10%, but revenues of $1.60 billion missed forecasts by 3.40% with an 18.32% year-over-year decline. The company maintained its $8-$8.2B fiscal 2027 bookings guidance, supported by strong Grand Theft Auto VI preorders ahead of its November 19 launch. NBA 2K27 underperformed expectations despite 4 million units sold, while mobile titles showed mixed results. Management emphasized cost discipline and cash flow focus.

items.title: QMCO Q2 Earnings Call Centers on Tape Demand and Supply Limits
items.summary: Quantum Corporation (QMCO) reported hyperscale tape demand surged 2.6x year-over-year with a record ~$100M backlog, driven by AI-related data growth and infrastructure cost control needs. However, component availability remains a bottleneck limiting revenue upside. Q3 guidance of $91M (+22% YoY) depends on tape drive supply recovery, with IBM doubling production and Fujifilm expanding capacity. The company maintains a 43% gross margin target over 18 months while managing divergent customer trends across mid-market, enterprise, and hyperscale segments.

items.title: ZETA Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Higher Outlook
items.summary: Zeta Global reported Q3 2026 revenues of $492.7 million, up 46% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of 38 cents beating consensus estimates. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.853-$1.857 billion (42% growth) driven by accelerating Athena AI platform adoption, which now represents over 70% of revenues. Management highlighted expanding enterprise opportunities through AthenaOS and strategic partnerships with Palantir and OpenAI, while improving profitability with adjusted EBITDA up 55% and free cash flow up 73%.

items.title: AMD vs. Intel: Which Is the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock to Buy Right Now?
items.summary: AMD is outpacing Intel in the AI chip market with 97% year-over-year data center revenue growth compared to Intel's 78%. AMD expects data center revenue to more than double in 2027 with 80%+ overall revenue growth, significantly outpacing Intel's 13% guidance. Despite trading at similar valuations, AMD's projected 118% EPS growth in 2027 versus Intel's 20% makes it the better investment choice.

items.title: CME vs. PayPal: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares CME Group and PayPal as investment options for 2027. CME Group operates the leading derivatives marketplace with a strong 62% net margin and 6.4% revenue growth, while PayPal operates a massive 439-million-account network with a lower 15.8% net margin but trades at a significantly cheaper valuation (P/E of 11.45 vs. 24.97). Despite PayPal's attractive valuation, the author recommends CME Group for its superior revenue growth, higher profitability margins, and stronger historical performance over the past decade.

items.title: Is CNH Industrials Stock Worth Buying After Q3 2026 Results?
items.summary: CNH Industrial is strengthening its agricultural equipment business through precision technology investments and a planned construction equipment joint venture with Kobelco, which should generate ~$700 million in cash for debt reduction. However, weak regional demand (particularly in South America), tariff pressures, rising credit risks, and working capital challenges continue to constrain financial performance, leading to a neutral investment outlook.

items.title: CME vs. S&P Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares CME Group and S&P Global as investment options for 2027. CME operates the world's leading derivatives marketplace with an impressive 62% net margin and pays a higher dividend yield of 1.68%. S&P Global provides critical credit ratings and financial data with more diversified revenue streams and higher absolute revenue ($15.3B vs $6.5B). Despite CME's superior profitability metrics, the author recommends S&P Global because CME has underperformed the S&P 500 by over 100 percentage points over the past decade, suggesting the trend may not reverse.

items.title: Time to Buy Nvidia-Heavy ETFs as CEO Huang's Affair Turns Into a Spy Plot?
items.summary: NVIDIA shares fell 4.3% ($193 billion in market value) following CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an extramarital affair and a board investigation into potential foreign espionage. While NVIDIA's AI fundamentals remain strong with 106% revenue growth, succession uncertainty and key-man risk pose near-term concerns. The article recommends NVIDIA-heavy ETFs as a diversified alternative to direct stock ownership to mitigate single-stock volatility.

items.title: Can ConocoPhillips Sustain Future Production Growth With Lower CapEx?
items.summary: ConocoPhillips plans to achieve low-single-digit production growth in 2027 while reducing capital spending, leveraging operational efficiencies in its Permian Basin assets and recently commissioned Canadian operations. The company targets a $7 billion free cash flow improvement by 2029 through cost reductions and efficiency gains, despite inflationary pressures on fuel, logistics, and chemicals.

items.title: Sandisk Stock Has Collapsed by 65%, but It's Still Undergoing an 8-for-1 Stock Split on Nov. 19. Here's Why I'm Still Not Buying Shares Amidst This Nasdaq Market Slump.
items.summary: SanDisk stock has plummeted 65% from its June peak despite strong current financials driven by AI infrastructure demand and memory chip shortages. While the stock appears cheap at a P/E of 3.5, the author warns investors to avoid buying ahead of the November 19 stock split, citing the cyclical nature of the memory chip market. The author projects that when supply normalizes and pricing power diminishes, SanDisk's earnings could collapse significantly, making the stock potentially overvalued at current levels.

items.title: BigBear.ai Expands Gross Margin by 878 Bps: What Drives the Gains?
items.summary: BigBear.ai (BBAI) reported Q3 2026 gross margin expansion of 878 basis points to 31.2% with 31% revenue growth to $43.6 million, driven by its generative AI platform adoption across federal agencies. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $150-$165 million and increased backlog to $330 million. However, adjusted EBITDA remains negative at $9.1 million, and the company faces intense competition from larger rivals like Palantir with significantly higher margins.

items.title: Newmont Stock Up 26% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Newmont (NEM) shares have gained 25.8% YTD, outperforming peers and the S&P 500, driven by higher realized gold prices and operational efficiency. The company is advancing key growth projects like Cadia Panel Caves and Tanami Expansion while maintaining strong liquidity of $12.8 billion. However, declining gold production (9% YoY in Q3) and rising costs pose headwinds to profitability, despite reduced 2026 cost guidance. Zacks rates NEM as a Hold.

items.title: Manufacturers Expanding Microsoft 365 Copilot Should Review Superseded Drawings and Supplier Permissions
items.summary: eSoftware Associates advises manufacturers implementing Microsoft 365 Copilot to establish proper document management controls before expansion. The company recommends five key steps: marking approved drawings with version metadata, retaining older revisions under appropriate access rules, limiting discovery during governance reviews, auditing supplier permissions, and reviewing access at project closeout. This guidance addresses security concerns highlighted by the 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report, which found third parties tied to 61% of manufacturing breaches.

items.title: Why Lockheed Martin Rallied in October
items.summary: Lockheed Martin shares rallied 25.1% in October following strong Q3 earnings that beat expectations and long-term procurement agreements with the Department of Defense. The company reported 11.3% revenue growth to $20.7 billion and 14.6% EPS growth to $7.95, while raising full-year guidance. Key drivers included strong performance in the Aeronautics division (F-35 fighter jets) and Missiles and Fire Control segments, along with a 10-year F-35 agreement guaranteeing minimum 850 aircraft sales and accelerated Joint Advanced Tactical Missile production.

items.title: What's Wrong With Kimberly-Clark Stock?
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark's stock has significantly underperformed the S&P 500 over the past five years, dropping 16.5% while the index gained 56.5%. The company faces sluggish sales growth (1.7% on a comparable basis in 2025, declining further to -1.3% in Q3 2026), margin compression, and competitive pricing pressures. While the recent acquisition of Kenvue adds brands like Tylenol and Listerine, the integration risks are substantial given the company's already-challenged sales environment.

items.title: Pfizer Hits a New 52-Week High. Here's Why It's Not Too Late to Buy the Stock
items.summary: Pfizer has outperformed the broader market in 2026, rising 18% year-to-date and hitting a new 52-week high. Despite the stock's gains, it remains undervalued with a forward P/E ratio of just 10. The company's recently launched and acquired products showed impressive 32% growth in the latest quarter, demonstrating successful portfolio expansion. With a 5.9% dividend yield and strong drug pipeline, Pfizer presents a compelling long-term buy-and-hold opportunity for investors.

items.title: Altria Yields Nearly 6%. Here's Why I'd Buy It for a Lifetime of Passive Income.
items.summary: Altria Group offers an attractive 5.66% dividend yield with a strong track record of 61 dividend increases over 57 years. The tobacco company generates substantial cash flow from its established Marlboro brand and is diversifying into smoke-free alternatives like nicotine pouches through its on! brand. Trading at a forward P/E of 13x, it presents a compelling opportunity for income investors despite facing long-term headwinds from declining cigarette consumption and regulatory pressures.
