items.title: Cadence Design Systems: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 21% growth and reported record backlog of $8.2 billion in Q3 2026. The company launched Maestro, an AI-specialized suite for semiconductor design, and saw accelerating demand for hardware verification tools as chip complexity increases. Management highlighted strong customer R&D investments and structural competitive advantages positioning the company well in the AI-driven semiconductor market.

items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb’s Cancer Drug Just Doubled Survival Time Without Progression — Here’s Why It Matters
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb announced positive Phase 3 trial results for izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren), an experimental cancer drug that doubled progression-free survival time (11.1 months vs. 5.7 months) compared to chemotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer patients. However, the stock reaction was muted because the trial was conducted only in China, and FDA approval typically requires multi-region confirmatory data meeting Western standards. The drug represents part of BMY's strategy to transition from legacy medications to a growth portfolio.

items.title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth
items.summary: NVIDIA and Meta announced an expanded partnership to optimize infrastructure for AI agents, particularly Meta's Muse models. Meta will deploy NVIDIA's Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X networking, and BlueField-4 technology. NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering. The collaboration aims to improve inference and training performance while enhancing security and monitoring capabilities for AI agent deployment.

items.title: Elon Musk Predicts a Wave of Failures Among AI Cloud Companies. Is SpaceX Stock a Sell?
items.summary: Elon Musk warned that debt markets have cut off lending to AI cloud companies without significant revenue outside data centers, predicting most of 200+ neoclouds will fail or be acquired. SpaceX's AI segment now represents 52% of revenue ($7.56B in Q3), but the company differs from struggling neoclouds due to profitable Starlink and launch businesses providing $7B in quarterly revenue. While SpaceX faces high capital spending ($35-40B forecasted for Q4), its investment-grade credit rating and profitable AI unit suggest it's not a sell, though the stock at 34x sales isn't a bargain.

items.title: Alphabet Must Show This on Oct. 28 or the Stock Could Stall
items.summary: Alphabet's Oct. 28 earnings report will be critical for investors to assess whether Google Cloud's growing profits are translating into actual cash flow. The company posted negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion in Q2 despite strong cloud growth, and is now spending more on capex ($195-205B annually) than it generates in operating cash flow ($185.7B over trailing 12 months). Investors should focus on whether operating cash flow returns to the $45-50 billion range to confirm the AI investment is self-funding, or if the company continues relying on shareholder capital.

items.title: Tesla Is Investing Aggressively in its Next Generation Technology
items.summary: Tesla is making significant capital expenditure investments in next-generation technologies including driverless/autonomous driving capabilities and robotics. However, these heavy investments are currently causing the company's profits to decline as it prioritizes long-term technology development over near-term profitability.

items.title: ROSEN, TRUSTED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Duolingo, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - DUOL
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. alleging that the company made materially false statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates. The lawsuit claims Duolingo deliberately added user friction through increased ads and subscription upsells while knowing this would negatively impact DAU growth, and that AI-generated content degraded product quality. Investors who purchased DUOL stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 may be eligible for compensation, with a December 7, 2026 deadline to serve as lead plaintiff.

items.title: Anthropic's Billions in Microsoft Commitments Add to Its Mounting Compute Bill
items.summary: Anthropic faces over $400 billion in cloud infrastructure commitments across multiple providers, with Microsoft alone accounting for at least $44.9 billion through 2033. The AI startup spent nearly $9 billion on compute in the first half of 2026, representing its largest cost. While these massive commitments pose risks if demand falters, they reflect the scarcity of computing power needed to support Anthropic's growth in generative AI.

items.title: ROSEN, A TOP-RANKED AND GLOBAL LAW FIRM, Encourages Baidu, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BIDU
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is soliciting investors who purchased securities in Baidu, Tigo Energy, and XTI Aerospace during specified class periods to join securities class action lawsuits. The firm alleges that Baidu overstated its AI business capabilities and misled investors about revenue prospects, while similar claims are being pursued against the other companies.

items.title: XTIA DEADLINE NOTICE: ROSEN, NATIONAL TRIAL LAWYERS, Encourages XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 27 Deadline in Securities Class Action - XTIA
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against XTI Aerospace, Inc. for investors who purchased securities between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities requiring Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to file timely earnings reports. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 27, 2026.

items.title: Why Range Resources Stock Surged Today
items.summary: Range Resources stock jumped nearly 18% after announcing an all-stock acquisition deal by EQT, creating a natural gas giant valued at over $50 billion. The merged company expects $325 million in annual cost savings and $20 billion in free cash flow over five years, positioning it to capitalize on rising LNG demand in Asia and Europe, plus growing natural gas demand from AI data centers.

items.title: Roper Technologies: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Roper Technologies reported 8% total revenue growth in Q3 2026 and raised full-year earnings expectations. The company is expanding AI agents into specialized enterprise workflows, has over $6 billion in acquisition capacity, and maintains enterprise software retention in the mid-90s, positioning it well for disciplined M&A and shareholder returns.

items.title: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) Laps the Stock Market: Here's Why
items.summary: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) closed at $12.79, up 2.65%, outperforming the S&P 500's 0.7% gain. The stock has gained 17% over the past month despite the sector declining 7.7%. Upcoming earnings are projected at -$0.22 per share with quarterly revenue expected at $53.09 million, down 29.36% year-over-year. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Principal Financial (PFG) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Miss Estimates
items.summary: Principal Financial (PFG) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.22 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $2.46 and representing a -9.76% earnings surprise. Revenue also fell short at $4.28 billion versus the $4.31 billion estimate. The company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revisions, with shares expected to underperform the market. Despite outperforming the S&P 500 by 23.1% year-to-date, the Insurance - Multi line industry ranks in the bottom 22% of Zacks industries.

items.title: Tesla Isn’t a Hyperscaler. Why the AI Bears Are Misreading Its $5 Billion Capex Cut.
items.summary: Tesla reduced its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $5 billion to approximately $20 billion, but this doesn't signal a pullback from AI development. Unlike hyperscalers like Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft that build data centers for external customers, Tesla's AI investments are focused on developing autonomous driving, robotaxi services, and humanoid robots for internal use. Management indicated spending will increase in coming years, suggesting the cut reflects timing rather than reduced ambition.

items.title: AI Headlines Pile Up as Wall Street Navigates a Volatile Week
items.summary: Anthropic filed for IPO with impressive financials showing $4.6B revenue in 2024 and $16.3B in H1 2026, while Meta announced a $95B equity offering to fund AI expansion. SpaceX secured $40B in debt financing for AI chips, but concerns mount over neocloud operators' sustainability as debt markets tighten. The AI investment cycle is shifting from infrastructure buildout to financing sustainability, with major central bank decisions and hyperscaler earnings reports this week adding to market volatility.

items.title: Deadline Alert: XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors Have Until October 27, 2026 to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role in Securities Fraud Class Action, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Reminds Investors
items.summary: XTI Aerospace investors have until October 27, 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status in a securities fraud class action lawsuit. The company failed to disclose material adverse facts about senior executives' undisclosed activities and governance issues, leading to a 15.9% stock price drop on August 18, 2026 when the company announced it could not timely file its quarterly report.

items.title: Elon Musk Warns of “Death and Consolidation” Across the AI Cloud Industry. Is SpaceX Really Different?
items.summary: Elon Musk warns that tightening debt markets are forcing widespread failures and consolidation among AI cloud providers ('neoclouds'). While SpaceX has diversified revenue streams that provide protection from this financing crunch, its AI infrastructure investments remain unproven and must eventually generate sufficient returns to justify their enormous costs.

items.title: Top Stock Picks for Week of October 26, 2026
items.summary: Zacks has identified Shopify (SHOP) and Penguin Solutions (PENG) as Zacks Rank #1 stocks with strong growth prospects. Shopify, a leading commerce platform, is expected to grow earnings 61.5% this fiscal year with improving free cash flow margins. Penguin Solutions, an AI infrastructure provider, reported Q4 EPS more than doubled year-over-year with revenue up 68%, and raised its fiscal 2027 guidance to 40% growth with 55% EPS growth at the midpoint.

items.title: FIX Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Backlog Growth and 2027 Outlook
items.summary: Comfort Systems USA (FIX) reported third-quarter revenues of $3.77B, exceeding consensus estimates, with a record $17.81B backlog representing 90% year-over-year growth. The company projects mid-40% organic growth in 2026 and mid-20% growth in 2027, driven by strong demand from technology customers who now represent 59% of revenues. Management is expanding modular capacity to 6M square feet by 2027 while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and selective customer commitments.

items.title: Vertiv to Report Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Vertiv is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 28, with expected revenues of $3.76 billion (40.63% YoY growth) and EPS of $1.82 (46.77% YoY growth). The company is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure and data center demand, margin expansion to 24-25%, and geographic strength across Americas, APAC, and EMEA. However, supply chain challenges and higher tariffs pose headwinds. Despite a stretched valuation at 15.72X price-to-book, Zacks rates VRT as a Buy (Rank #2) based on robust growth prospects and AI innovation.

items.title: Is REAL a Buy Now as Growth Accelerates but Valuation Stays Rich?
items.summary: The RealReal (REAL) reported Q2 2026 GMV growth of 22% to $617M and doubled adjusted EBITDA, raising its 2026 outlook. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (10.96X forward PEG) with concerns around take-rate compression, high debt levels, and competition from eBay and ThredUp in the resale market.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alphabet Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding Gemini 3.5 Pro's performance. The complaint claims the AI model delivered disappointing training results, leading to significant launch delays, while the company made positive statements about its business prospects that lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026.

items.title: Masco to Report Q3 Earnings: Here's What to Expect This Season
items.summary: Masco Corporation is set to report Q3 2026 results on October 28, with EPS estimated at $1.01 (up 4.1% YoY) and sales projected to grow 0.8%. The Decorative Architectural Products segment is expected to drive growth with 9.8% sales increase, while Plumbing Products may decline 2.3%. The company's restructuring initiatives and cost controls should support margins, though the stock carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with no earnings beat predicted.

items.title: Here's What Investors Must Know Ahead of BigBear.ai's Q3 Earnings
items.summary: BigBear.ai is expected to report Q3 2026 revenues of $38.9 million, up 17.5% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AI solutions in defense and border operations. However, the company is forecast to report a loss of six cents per share, narrower than the prior year but wider than consensus estimates from 30 days ago. While higher-margin GenAI products like Ask Sage may help reduce losses, rising R&D and operational expenses are expected to pressure profitability.

items.title: Equinix to Post Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: Equinix (EQIX) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 28, with consensus estimates projecting 11% revenue growth to $2.57 billion and 6.9% AFFO per share growth to $10.51. Strong demand for interconnected data center infrastructure driven by AI adoption and cloud expansion is expected to support growth, though high interest expenses may be a headwind. The company's quantitative model does not predict a surprise beat this quarter.

items.title: BXP to Post Q3 Earnings: Is the Stock a Portfolio Must-Have?
items.summary: BXP, Inc. is scheduled to report Q3 2026 results on October 27, with revenues projected to rise 3.7% and FFO per share expected to grow 3.5% year-over-year. The office REIT is positioned to benefit from strong demand for premier office spaces and positive U.S. office market recovery, though competitive leasing conditions and higher operating costs may limit margin expansion.

items.title: Salesforce vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Salesforce and IBM present contrasting investment profiles in 2026. Salesforce leads in growth (13.5% vs 4.5% average revenue growth) and profitability (21.5% operating margin), while IBM offers better valuation metrics (3.4x P/S ratio vs 4.7x) and higher dividend yield (2.66% vs 0.70%). The choice depends on investor preference: growth-oriented investors favor Salesforce, while value investors may prefer IBM.

items.title: Intuit vs. BILL: Which Financial Software Stock Is a Better Buy Today?
items.summary: Intuit and BILL Holdings both compete in the financial software space, with different strategies. Intuit leverages its QuickBooks platform and broader diversification, but faces slowing customer growth and declining EPS estimates. BILL focuses on payment workflows with stronger profitability prospects (23-24% operating margin expected in FY27) and positive EPS revisions. BILL trades at a lower forward P/E multiple and is rated a Strong Buy, while Intuit is rated Buy, with BILL offering stronger growth and profitability improvement potential.

items.title: Fortinet Stock Before Q3 Earnings: Buy Now or Wait for Results?
items.summary: Fortinet is set to report Q3 2026 results with projected revenues of $2.01-$2.1B (19.55% YOY growth) and billings of $2.25-$2.35B. Strong demand for SASE Firewall, AI-security expansion through the Virtue AI acquisition, and strategic partnerships with Intel support growth. However, premium valuation (P/E of 47.69), margin pressures, and intense competition from established cybersecurity players present headwinds.

items.title: Not AMD. Not Marvell. Here's Which Company Nvidia Needs to Be Worried About.
items.summary: Broadcom, not AMD or Marvell, poses the biggest threat to Nvidia's AI computing dominance through custom AI chips. With AI segment revenue expected to reach $115 billion in 2027 and $230 billion in 2028, Broadcom is positioned to capture significant market share. Trading at 17x 2027 earnings estimates, the stock could potentially double if valued at 35x earnings, offering strong growth potential alongside multiple years of revenue expansion.

items.title: Glacier Bancorp: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Glacier Bancorp reported record quarterly net income of $105 million in Q3 2026, driven by higher yields on new loans and expanding profit margins. The bank's net interest margin surpassed 4% as $3.5 billion in maturing loans will reprice higher over the next year. Strong growth in noninterest-bearing deposits at a 15% annualized rate is lowering funding costs, while accumulating capital reserves are prompting management to evaluate share buybacks and special dividends.

items.title: Can Synopsys' AI Push Drive Chip Design Efficiency and Growth?
items.summary: Synopsys (SNPS) is capitalizing on rising demand for advanced chip design tools by integrating AI agents across its EDA portfolio to automate engineering workflows. The company reported 82% recurring revenues, a $10.9 billion backlog, and raised fiscal 2026 guidance to $9.69-$9.74 billion. However, SNPS faces competitive pressures from Cadence and Keysight, elevated debt from the Ansys acquisition, and trades at a premium valuation of 7.53X forward P/S versus the industry average of 6.27X.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Innventure, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) and its officers for alleged securities fraud. The complaint alleges that the company made false and misleading statements regarding its subsidiary Accelsius's deal with DarkNX, claiming the transformative deal was unlikely to materialize and that revenue targets for 2026 were not reasonably plausible. Investors who purchased Innventure securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 are encouraged to join the case.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has 69% of Berkshire Hathaway's Portfolio Invested in Just 5 Stocks. Here's My Top Pick for October.
items.summary: Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO, has concentrated the portfolio into 5 stocks representing 69% of holdings, down from 42 to 29 total positions. Abel has aggressively increased Alphabet holdings from 2% to 9.4% in just one year, similar to how Warren Buffett built Apple into the largest position. Despite high capital expenditures, Alphabet's attractive 16x P/E ratio and $514 billion cloud backlog make it an appealing investment during the AI boom.

items.title: Generac to Report Q3 Earnings: Should Investors Hold or Fold?
items.summary: Generac (GNRC) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on Oct. 28 with expected revenue growth of 17.9% to $1.31 billion. The company's data center business is accelerating with a $1.6 billion backlog and a major $2.4 billion Amazon supply deal, but residential segment weakness, margin pressures from product mix, and capacity expansion execution risks warrant caution. The stock has underperformed its industry over the past six months.

items.title: EQT Is Building a $50 Billion Natural Gas Giant as AI Power Demand Surges
items.summary: EQT is acquiring Range Resources in an all-stock deal to create a $50 billion natural gas giant, positioning itself as the largest U.S. gas producer with over 9 Bcfe/d production capacity. The merger is driven by surging AI data center power demand, with EQT strategically locking in long-term supply agreements at premium prices. However, the company faces risks from potential AI infrastructure slowdown.

items.title: Intel and TSMC Are Vying for Chip Fabrication Supremacy. 1 Offers Superior Value.
items.summary: While Intel's foundry business is showing growth momentum with recent government and Nvidia investments, TSMC remains the superior value investment. Intel's foundry division operates at a 36% loss with a forward P/E of 44x, compared to TSMC's 59% operating margin and 18x P/E ratio. Despite Intel's turnaround narrative gaining market attention, TSMC's profitability and valuation make it the more attractive choice for investors.

items.title: HPE vs. AGYS: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is positioned as the superior value investment compared to Agilysys (AGYS) based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook. HPE has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 14.88 and PEG ratio of 0.44, while AGYS carries a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 50.08 and PEG ratio of 2.50. HPE received a Value grade of B versus AGYS's F grade.

items.title: Adobe vs. Datadog: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Adobe and Datadog represent two different investment approaches in cloud software: Adobe offers established profitability with a 30% net margin and $9.9B free cash flow at an 11.1x forward P/E, while Datadog delivers rapid 27.7% revenue growth but trades at a premium 101.7x forward P/E with minimal profitability. Adobe suits value-focused investors prioritizing profits and affordability, while Datadog appeals to growth-oriented investors willing to pay for expansion potential.

items.title: Xylem Gears Up to Post Q3 Earnings: What's in the Cards?
items.summary: Xylem Inc. (XYL) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 27, with revenue expected to grow only 0.4% to $2.28 billion and earnings per share projected at $1.47 (up 7.3% YoY). While infrastructure demand, data-center growth, and the TriOS acquisition support revenues, project delays, rising costs, and inflationary pressures cloud the outlook. The company carries a negative Earnings ESP of -1.27% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), suggesting limited likelihood of beating consensus estimates.

items.title: Citigroup Lifts 2026 RoTCE Outlook: What's Fueling the Optimism?
items.summary: Citigroup raised its 2026 return on tangible common equity (RoTCE) outlook to above 11% from 10-11%, driven by strong Q3 results with 11.5% RoTCE. Services and Wealth revenues grew 15% each, while the efficiency ratio improved to 58.5%. The company targets 11-13% RoTCE for 2027-2028 and 14-15% medium-term, supported by ongoing restructuring and operational improvements.

items.title: WCN Stock Gains 11% After Reporting Q3 Earnings & Revenue Beat
items.summary: Waste Connections (WCN) exceeded Q3 earnings and revenue expectations, driven by 5.5% core pricing growth, 3% landfill volume increase, and stronger recycling revenues. The company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $10.09B and increased its quarterly dividend by 10%, causing shares to gain 10.9% post-earnings.

items.title: Investors Are Avoiding This Industry Like the Plague. Berkshire Is Going All In. Should You Invest?
items.summary: The U.S. housing industry is struggling with pending home sales down 7.3% month-over-month and 11.3% year-over-year, causing investors to flee homebuilder stocks. However, Berkshire Hathaway is making significant investments in the sector, including acquiring Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion and increasing its stake in Lennar to 11%. Berkshire CEO Greg Abel views the 10-million-home housing shortage as a long-term opportunity, though he cautions recovery won't be quick. The article suggests ordinary investors should consider buying Berkshire shares rather than directly investing in homebuilders given the volatility and patience required.

items.title: Netflix Co-CEO Greg Peters Just Said "We Know That We Can Do Better" When It Comes to U.S. Engagement. Should Investors Be Worried?
items.summary: Netflix reported Q3 earnings ahead of consensus but disappointed investors with lower full-year revenue guidance. Co-CEO Greg Peters acknowledged the company can improve U.S. engagement, citing it as an opportunity rather than a crisis. While engagement is strong in Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and EMEA regions, the U.S. market shows softer trends. The stock has declined 47% over the past year amid investor concerns about competition from short-form content and potential AI disruption to content creation costs.

items.title: Gen Digital to Report Q2 Earnings: What's in the Cards for the Stock?
items.summary: Gen Digital (GEN) is scheduled to report Q2 FY2027 results on Oct. 28, expecting revenues of $1.325-$1.350 billion and EPS of 71-73 cents. The company has blocked over 500 million scam attacks in Q1 and its Engine Marketplace reached a $500 million revenue run rate. Growth is expected to be driven by sustained demand for cybersecurity solutions amid rising AI-enabled threats, expansion of AI-driven products like Norton Neo, and the Engine Marketplace's partner additions.

items.title: AXP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Guidance Hike and AI Strategy
items.summary: American Express raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.60-$17.90, driven by resilient premium customer spending, 8% billed business growth, and 17% net card fee acceleration. The company is expanding AI capabilities across its membership model and plans to cut 5% of global positions to improve efficiency and investment capacity.

items.title: Verizon Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Strong Margins, Revenues Miss
items.summary: Verizon reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.31 per share, beating estimates by 3.15%, with revenues missing expectations. The company added 406,000 postpaid phone subscribers and raised its 2026 EPS outlook to $5.04-$5.06. Strong service revenue growth, improved margins, and robust cash flow supported the results, though broadband additions slowed slightly.

items.title: Are Utilities Stocks Lagging  Consolidated Edison (ED) This Year?
items.summary: Consolidated Edison (ED) has returned 16.5% year-to-date, significantly outperforming the Utilities sector average of 1.3%. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook. Enel Chile (ENIC) is also highlighted as an outperformer in the same industry with an 8% year-to-date return.

items.title: CVS Health Q3 Earnings Preview: How to Approach the Stock?
items.summary: CVS Health is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings on Nov. 4 with modest EPS growth of 1.3% to $1.62 and revenue growth of 2.1% to $105.04 billion. While Aetna margin recovery and Government business strength are positive, the company faces headwinds from elevated medical costs, 340B pharmacy pressures, and membership declines. CVS's $20 billion technology investment and strong earnings beat history provide some optimism, though near-term challenges persist.

items.title: Verizon Communications (VZ) Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates
items.summary: Verizon Communications reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.31 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.27, but revenues of $34.31 billion missed expectations by 1.43%. The company has underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date (9.7% vs 11.4%). With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, the stock is expected to perform in line with the market. ATN International is also mentioned as an upcoming earnings reporter in the same industry.

items.title: Boeing vs. Airbus: Which Stock Offers Greater Upside Potential?
items.summary: Boeing and Airbus, the leading global aircraft manufacturers, are positioned to benefit from growing air travel demand and defense spending. Boeing shows stronger near-term momentum with Q3 delivery growth, FAA certification of the 737-10 aircraft, and significantly higher earnings growth forecasts (89.85% YoY). Airbus is diversifying through defense integration capabilities and aviation services market expansion projected to double by 2045. Despite both stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating, Boeing is favored for its better valuation, price performance, and earnings outlook.

items.title: Regeneron Extends Agreement with BARDA to Provide Additional Supply of Ebola Treatment Inmazeb® for U.S. Preparedness
items.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals has extended its agreement with BARDA to supply additional doses of Inmazeb, its FDA-approved Ebola treatment, through 2031 for approximately $270 million. The company is also advancing maftivimab, a component of Inmazeb, as a potential monotherapy treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease in the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

items.title: AutoZone Chief Financial Officer Jamere Jackson to Depart November 25, 2026
items.summary: AutoZone announced that Chief Financial Officer Jamere Jackson is resigning effective November 25, 2026, to become CFO of FedEx Corporation. Jackson served AutoZone for six years and contributed to record sales, earnings, and EPS growth. The company has commenced an external search for his successor and expressed confidence in its finance team's ability to ensure continuity.

items.title: GE Vernova Reports Oct. 28. Here's the 1 Number That Matters More Than Its Multibillion-Dollar Backlog (Hint: It's Measured in Gigawatts).
items.summary: GE Vernova's $176 billion backlog is impressive, but investors should focus on gigawatts of gas power capacity, particularly HA-class heavy-duty gas turbines. These turbines generate $500 million in high-margin service revenue per GW over 20 years. The company expects 400 HA machines running or on contract by end of 2027, with guidance for 20-40 GW orders in the second half of 2026. Strong HA turbine orders could significantly boost the stock.

items.title: Prediction: Broadcom Will Be a $4.5 Trillion Company by 2030
items.summary: Broadcom is positioned to become a $4.5 trillion company by 2030, driven by explosive growth in custom AI processors and optical networking components. The company expects AI revenue to reach $230 billion in fiscal 2028 with 186% growth in fiscal 2026. With projected EPS reaching $51.36 by 2030 and potential stock price of $1,027, Broadcom could triple from current levels.

items.title: $BAC Stock Losses: BFA Law Reminds Bank of America Investors with Losses of the Ongoing Securities Fraud Class Action Over $1.21 Billion in Penalties
items.summary: Bank of America faces a securities fraud class action lawsuit after the U.S. Treasury Department announced over $1.21 billion in penalties for violations of sanctions and anti-money laundering laws. The company's stock dropped 4.8% on October 14, 2026, following the announcement. Investors allege that Bank of America misrepresented the scope and financial consequences of its Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering compliance failures. The lead plaintiff deadline is December 15, 2026.

items.title: Alphabet Has $514 Billion in Cloud Orders. Here’s What Matters More Than That Number on Oct. 28.
items.summary: Alphabet's Google Cloud backlog reached $514 billion, demonstrating strong AI demand. However, investors should focus on cloud margins, capital expenditure efficiency, and Search revenue growth when the company reports Q3 earnings on Oct. 28, rather than the backlog figure alone. The company faces margin pressure from third-party capacity usage and massive capex spending, but its profitable advertising business and AI investments position it well long-term.

items.title: The Nasdaq Composite Just Plunged Almost 700 Points in One Day: Is a Stock Market Crash Imminent?
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite dropped 694 points (2.6%) on October 22, 2026, marking its largest daily decline since June. While the stock market has rallied significantly since 2022 driven by AI infrastructure spending, historical indicators suggest elevated crash risk: the S&P 500's CAPE Ratio near 43 (vs. historical average of 17.44) and margin debt at record $1.502 trillion. However, the article emphasizes that downturns are normal and historically resolve quickly, with bull markets lasting 3.6 times longer than bear markets on average.

items.title: Bull of the Day: Hasbro (HAS)
items.summary: Hasbro (HAS) posted strong quarterly results with revenue climbing 15% YoY to $1.6 billion and adjusted EPS up 72% YoY. Magic: The Gathering sales surpassed $600 million for the first time, up 34% YoY. The company raised FY26 guidance and doubled its share buyback target. Shares have surged over 30% in the last three months, earning a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating.

items.title: FTI Consulting Adds Björn Storim to Strengthen Banking and Capital Markets Advisory in Germany
items.summary: FTI Consulting announced the appointment of Björn Storim, former CEO of BNY's European Bank, as a Senior Advisor in its Strategic Communications segment based in Frankfurt. With 35 years of international financial services experience, Storim will advise on banking, capital markets, regulation, and strategic transformation challenges for financial institutions across the EMEA region.

items.title: Barmeter Technologies Issues Statement on Harsha Nooka’s Research on Accessible AI-Generated Web Interfaces
items.summary: Barmeter Technologies highlighted published research by Harsha Vardhan Reddy Nooka on the accessibility of AI-generated web interfaces. The AXIS-Bench pilot study evaluated whether large language models can generate code that meets WCAG 2.2 and WAI-ARIA standards. Results showed that AI-generated code with accessibility guidance passed all 12 interactivity tests, while baseline and single-pass conditions performed poorly, emphasizing the importance of functional accessibility evaluation beyond visual design.

items.title: Chip Stocks to Buy After Their Worst Day Since June
items.summary: The semiconductor index fell 6.7% on Oct. 22, its worst day since June, with major chip stocks declining sharply. However, the sell-off appears to be a buying opportunity, as the decline was triggered by supply constraints rather than weak demand. Lam Research reported record revenue and expects industry equipment spending to exceed $200 billion by 2027. Micron, AMD, and Marvell all maintain positive outlooks despite the stock price declines, with none cutting guidance.

items.title: ROSEN, A LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages AppLovin Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action – APP
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is soliciting investors who purchased AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ: APP) securities between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026 to join a class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that AppLovin made false statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstated AI model improvements, and misrepresented the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. The lead plaintiff deadline is November 16, 2026.

items.title: The Cooper Companies, Inc. Investor News: If You Have Suffered Losses in The Cooper Companies, Inc., You Are Encouraged to Contact The Rosen Law Firm About Your Rights
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is investigating potential securities claims against The Cooper Companies, Inc. (NASDAQ: COO) for allegedly issuing materially misleading business information. The investigation was prompted by Cooper Companies' disappointing earnings report on September 10, 2026, which included weak guidance and a decision not to sell Cooper Surgical, causing the stock to fall 14.6% that day. Investors who purchased Cooper Companies securities may be eligible for compensation through a class action lawsuit.

items.title: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF Long-Term Outlook: What Historical Trends Suggest for Patient Investors
items.summary: The S&P 500 has historically returned roughly 10% annually despite major market crises. While current earnings growth of 29% year-over-year driven by AI is unsustainable and could lead to below-average returns in the near term, long-term investors should benefit from the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF's broad market exposure and minimal 0.03% expense ratio. Corporate earnings growth remains the key long-term driver of stock prices.

items.title: BULL INVESTOR ALERT: RGRD Law Announces that Webull Corporation Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead Shareholder Class Action Lawsuit - December 7, 2026 Deadline
items.summary: Webull Corporation faces a securities class action lawsuit alleging the company made false statements about its independence from China. A U.S. House Select Committee found that Webull's ownership, workforce, and infrastructure are structurally tied to the People's Republic of China, contradicting the company's claims of being an American-based operation. The stock fell 19% following the October 7, 2026 CNBC report. Investors with substantial losses can seek lead plaintiff status by December 7, 2026.

items.title: VeriSign: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: VeriSign reported record domain registrations of 13.1 million in Q3 2026, with domain base reaching 183 million names. The company raised full-year growth guidance to 6.5-7% driven by AI-accelerated website creation. Key growth catalysts include the upcoming .web launch in early 2027 with flexible pricing, and the new VeriSign Informed security credential service launching in H1 2027. The company returned $1.14 billion to shareholders over twelve months.

items.title: ASTS INVESTOR ALERT: RGRD Law Announces that AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead Class Action Lawsuit Before November 13, 2026 Deadline
items.summary: AST SpaceMobile faces a securities class action lawsuit alleging that company executives made false and misleading statements regarding capital requirements, competitive position in the satellite direct-to-cellular market, and user adoption rates. Investors with substantial losses can seek lead plaintiff status before the November 13, 2026 deadline. The lawsuit covers the period from March 4, 2025 to July 15, 2026.

items.title: Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) Alert: Securities Class Action Pending, Investors with Losses Encouraged to Contact Hagens Berman Before November 2, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline
items.summary: Hims & Hers Health faces a securities class action lawsuit following an FTC federal complaint alleging deceptive health data sharing with third-party advertising platforms and ROSCA violations related to subscription billing practices. The allegations caused HIMS stock to plunge $4.32 (-14.7%) on July 29, 2026, erasing over $970 million in market capitalization. Investors with losses are encouraged to contact Hagens Berman before the November 2, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

items.title: Realty Income Yields More Than Quintuple the S&P 500. Here's What a $10,000 Investment Produces in Yearly Dividends.
items.summary: Realty Income (O) offers a forward dividend yield of 5.9%, more than five times the S&P 500's yield of under 1.1%. A $10,000 investment would generate approximately $583.54 annually in dividends. As a REIT required to distribute 90% of taxable income, Realty Income has maintained over 30 years of consecutive annual dividend increases, making it attractive for income-focused investors willing to accept slower price appreciation.

items.title: Airbnb vs. Coupang: Cyclical Volatility vs. Steady Scale in Revenue
items.summary: Airbnb and Coupang present contrasting revenue patterns: Airbnb experiences seasonal fluctuations typical of travel with consistent year-over-year growth, while Coupang maintains steadier revenue 2.5-3x higher than Airbnb. However, Coupang's growth is slowing following a major 2025 data breach and $400 million government fine, with year-over-year growth declining from 18% to 4% over recent quarters, suggesting reputational damage and customer acquisition challenges.

items.title: Investors Are Worried About Too Much AI Spending. They're Not Wrong, But It's Paying Off for These 2 Tech Stocks.
items.summary: While investors worry about excessive AI spending across the tech industry, Microsoft and Amazon are demonstrating tangible returns on their massive capital expenditures through their cloud services. AWS and Azure are experiencing strong revenue growth and profitability, with AWS at $169 billion annualized revenue and Azure at $100 billion. Microsoft is highlighted as having additional growth potential through its Copilot AI software ecosystem integrated with Azure.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reaffirms His $4 Trillion Projection for AI Spending. Here's Why That Makes Nvidia a Screaming Buy Now.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reaffirmed his projection that global data center capital expenditures will reach $3-4 trillion annually by 2030, up from an estimated $1 trillion this year. If Nvidia maintains its market share as the AI infrastructure market grows, the company could see revenue triple to quadruple to $1.2-1.6 trillion annually, potentially resulting in a market cap of $18-24 trillion compared to its current $5.4 trillion valuation.

items.title: Intel vs. SK Hynix: Revenue Trends to Help Investors Weigh Which Artificial Intelligence Stock to Buy
items.summary: SK Hynix has dramatically surpassed Intel in revenue growth over the past two years, reaching $52.6 billion in Q2 2026 compared to Intel's $16.1 billion, driven by massive demand for advanced memory semiconductors. While SK Hynix achieved historic profitability with a 76% operating margin, Intel is attempting a turnaround under new CEO Lip-Bu Tan, with Q2 2026 marking its highest quarterly sales in two years. The key question for investors is whether SK Hynix's exceptional growth will sustain or face margin pressure as manufacturing capacity expands.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against XTI Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: XTIA) alleging that company executives made materially false and misleading statements during the Class Period (April 15, 2026 - August 17, 2026). The complaint claims defendants failed to disclose undisclosed executive activities, issues with disclosure controls, and inability to timely file earnings reports. Investors who purchased XTI Aerospace securities during this period are encouraged to join the lawsuit, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bank of America Corporation for alleged violations of federal securities laws. The complaint alleges that BAC made false and misleading statements regarding systemic weaknesses in its Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering compliance program, failure to properly monitor trillions in transactions, and inadequate remediation of compliance deficiencies. Investors who purchased BAC securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 15, 2026.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: HONA) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm.
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA) alleging that the company made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts during the period of June 29, 2026 to September 1, 2026. The complaint alleges undisclosed supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, a false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts, and that positive statements about the company lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased securities during the class period may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 23, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm

The complaint claims the company made false statements regarding its capital requirements, competitive position in the satellite direct-to-cell market, and user adoption rates. Investors who purchased securities between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026 may be eligible to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 13, 2026.

items.title: Duolingo, Inc. (DUOL) Class Action Lawsuit: Investors Face December 7, 2026, Deadline - Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. for investors who purchased Class A common stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges material misstatements regarding the company's monetization strategy and growth prospects. Duolingo's stock declined significantly following disappointing DAU growth reports and strategic reversals, falling from $193.74 to $101 over three major announcements between November 2025 and February 2026. The deadline to seek lead plaintiff status is December 7, 2026.

items.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is Set to Cash in on AI. Here's What a $5,000 Investment Could Be Worth by 2030.
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) is positioned to benefit significantly from AI growth as the world's largest chip foundry. The article projects that a $5,000 investment could grow to approximately $15,000 by 2030, based on assumptions of 35% annual revenue growth, 50% profit margins, and a valuation multiple of 25x earnings. TSMC's dominance in producing cutting-edge chips for AI applications, combined with its $265 billion commitment to U.S. production capacity expansion, supports this bullish outlook.

items.title: Webull Corporation (BULL) Class Action Lawsuit: Investors Face December 7, 2026, Deadline - Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Webull Corporation for allegedly making material misstatements about its relationship with China. The company falsely represented its China operations as limited to R&D while actually depending heavily on PRC-based personnel and infrastructure. Following a CNBC report revealing that 62% of Webull's workforce is in mainland China despite claims of no Chinese offices, the stock fell 19% on October 7, 2026. Investors who purchased BULL securities between April 26, 2025 and October 6, 2026 have until December 7, 2026 to file for lead plaintiff status.

items.title: INV EQUITY ACTION REMINDER: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Reminds Innventure (NASDAQ: INV) Investors of Securities Class Action Lawsuit Deadline on October 27, 2026
items.summary: Innventure faces a securities class action lawsuit alleging the company made false statements about Accelsius' DarkNX AI data center project and overstated 2026 revenue targets. After a May 2026 report exposed the project as fabricated, the stock fell 8.42%. In August 2026, Innventure suspended its revenue targets and disclosed the DarkNX project was removed from internal bookings, causing a 55% stock price decline. Investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit with an October 27, 2026 deadline to seek lead plaintiff status.

items.title: Can GE Vernova's Gas Turbines Make Up for a Collapsing Wind Business?
items.summary: GE Vernova's wind turbine business is declining sharply with Q2 revenue down 11% and orders down 40%, but this is being offset by strong growth in its natural gas turbine business, which saw 14% revenue growth and 135% order growth. The company's total combined orders reached a record $24.2 billion in Q2, with only 20% of the power division backlog from AI data centers, reducing dependency on that sector.

items.title: XTIA EQUITY ACTION REMINDER: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Reminds XTI Aerospace Investors of Securities Class Action Lawsuit Deadline on October 27, 2026
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against XTI Aerospace (NASDAQ: XTIA) alleging that company executives made false and misleading statements about business operations while engaging in undisclosed activities. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased shares between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026. The alleged misconduct was revealed on August 17, 2026, when XTI Aerospace disclosed it could not timely file its Form 10-Q due to an internal review of its former CEO who resigned that day, resulting in a 15.9% stock price decline.

items.title: Breakfast News: The Sunday Edition
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang claims AGI has already arrived. The Motley Fool's Rule Breakers team selected five stocks positioned to benefit in an AGI world: Everpure for data management, Alphabet for its full-stack AI approach, Broadcom for networking and compute infrastructure, and ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor for chip manufacturing capabilities needed to support AGI-driven demand.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway Stock Rose 10 Days in a Row in October for the First Time Since 2018. Here's What History Says Comes Next.
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's Class B shares achieved 10 consecutive daily gains in October 2026 for the first time since 2018, rising from $498 to $526. Historical analysis shows that in 4 of 6 previous similar streaks, the stock traded higher 12 months later. Under new CEO Greg Abel, the company has demonstrated strong capital deployment through increased share buybacks ($4.4 billion), expanded positions in Alphabet and Delta Air Lines, and maintained substantial cash reserves, suggesting management confidence in the stock's value.

items.title: Libtayo® (cemiplimab) Longer-Term Data Show Increasing and Clinically Meaningful Overall Survival Benefit with Adjuvant Treatment in High-Risk Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (CSCC)
items.summary: Regeneron announced longer-term data (44-month follow-up) from the Phase 3 C-POST trial showing Libtayo (cemiplimab) as adjuvant treatment for high-risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma demonstrated a 37% reduction in risk of death compared to placebo, with sustained disease-free survival benefits. The drug was approved by the FDA in October 2025 and European Commission in November 2025 as the first immunotherapy for this indication.

items.title: SpaceX Just Shared Great News for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Investors. Here Are 2 Stocks That Could Benefit
items.summary: SpaceX reported strong Q3 results with its Super Intelligence segment revenue soaring 830% year-over-year to $7.6 billion, signaling robust demand for AI compute. The company's $16.4 billion capex in its AI business and CEO Elon Musk's prediction of a prolonged superintelligence compute shortage suggest sustained growth in AI infrastructure spending, benefiting GPU suppliers and AI compute rental companies.

items.title: Meet the Ultra-High-Yield Dividend Stock That Has Doubled the S&P 500's Returns This Year
items.summary: Altria (MO), the tobacco giant, has outperformed the S&P 500 by 28% to 13% year-to-date through October 12, 2026. With a 5.8% dividend yield and 57 consecutive years of dividend increases (Dividend King status), Altria appeals primarily to income investors. While declining smoking rates pose a long-term challenge, the company's pricing power and focus on earnings-per-share growth help sustain its dividend. Altria is expanding into smokeless nicotine products but lags competitors like Philip Morris International.

items.title: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Gets 96% of Product Sales From Treatments for 1 Disease. Here's Why That's About to Change.
items.summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is diversifying beyond its dominant cystic fibrosis franchise, which currently accounts for 96% of product sales. The company is expanding into new therapeutic areas through promising pipeline candidates including pain relief drug Journavx, gene-editing therapy Casgevy (with CRISPR Therapeutics), kidney disease therapy inaxaplin, and recent acquisitions like Crinetics Pharmaceuticals ($10 billion) for endocrine disease treatments. With Q2 revenue of $3.33 billion (up 12% YoY) and raised full-year guidance, Vertex expects $500 million+ in 2026 sales from new products.

items.title: Union Pacific Corporation: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Union Pacific reported record Q3 2026 financial results driven by operational efficiency and volume growth. The company maintained terminal dwell times below 20 hours for four consecutive quarters and achieved 13% domestic intermodal volume growth. A proposed merger with Norfolk Southern aims to create a transcontinental system that would reduce transit times and improve competitiveness against trucking.

items.title: Airbnb vs. Chewy: Do Pets or Places Power One Stock More than the Other?
items.summary: Airbnb and Chewy represent two different consumer discretionary growth stories. Airbnb boasts stronger profitability with a 20.4% net margin, a dominant marketplace with competitive moats, and expects $14.1B in revenue for 2026. Chewy offers stickier customer loyalty through its Autoship program and expanding pet health services, with more affordable valuation but faces regulatory complexity and weaker competitive positioning. The choice depends on preference between higher-growth tech-driven travel or steady pet retail expansion.

items.title: Abbott Laboratories vs. UnitedHealth: Does Health Innovation or Health Insurance Make for a Better Stock to Buy?
items.summary: The article compares Abbott Laboratories and UnitedHealth Group as healthcare investment options. Abbott, with $44.3B in revenue and a conservative 0.3x debt-to-equity ratio, focuses on medical devices, diagnostics, and pharmaceuticals, with planned growth from the Exact Sciences acquisition and a nutrition business spin-off. UnitedHealth, with $447.6B in revenue but higher leverage at 0.8x debt-to-equity, dominates insurance and healthcare services but faces government policy risks and reputational challenges. The author recommends Abbott for its innovation focus and lower exposure to healthcare cost-control initiatives.

items.title: Honeywell Technologies: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Honeywell raised its full-year profit and sales outlook following the completion of its aerospace business spin-off, positioning itself as a pure-play automation enterprise. The company reported a $19 billion order backlog, driven by strong demand in process automation from Middle East and Africa energy projects, accelerated elimination of stranded corporate overhead costs, and over 100% year-to-date order growth in data center infrastructure. Management expects continued strong performance in 2027 with improved cash conversion and increased capital allocation flexibility.

items.title: Why Hasbro Stock Surged This Week
items.summary: Hasbro stock surged 18.9% this week following a strong Q3 earnings report with revenue of $1.60 billion (beating estimates of $1.48 billion) and adjusted EPS of $2.90 (vs. expected $1.86). Magic: The Gathering drove growth with revenue jumping 34% year-over-year to exceed $600 million for the first time. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to 7%-9% growth and doubled share repurchase targets to $400 million, reflecting strong cash flow and a successful shift toward higher-margin digital and tabletop gaming.

items.title: HYLN DEADLINE TUESDAY: Hyliion Holdings Corp. Investors Have Until October 27th to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role with Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C.
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Hyliion Holdings Corp. for allegedly making false statements about a business deal with a recently formed entity lacking actual operations. The lawsuit claims CEO Thomas Healy and CFO Jon Panzer timed the announcement to facilitate insider trading, causing investor losses. The deadline to apply as lead plaintiff is October 27, 2026.

items.title: 2026 National Poppy Campaign launches with a donation “first” … and stunning mural: Don’t forget to Remember
items.summary: The Royal Canadian Legion launched its 2026 National Poppy Campaign with new tap-on-phone contactless donation technology supported by BMO. A 4x7 metre mural featuring handwritten messages from Canadians was unveiled at Union Station in Toronto, honoring WWI veteran Allan McLean Davidson. The campaign includes multiple donation methods through partners like RBC, Amazon Canada, Starbucks, and TD Bank, with proceeds supporting Canadian Veterans and their families.

items.title: Breakfast News: A Conversation With Moderna’s CEO
items.summary: Moderna's CEO Stéphane Bancel discusses the company's mRNA platform technology and its personalized cancer vaccine intismeran, which showed promising phase 3 trial results for melanoma when combined with Merck's Keytruda. The CEO emphasizes Moderna's platform approach, high clinical trial success rate (85% vs. 10% industry average), patent strategy, and long-term investment focus over quarterly earnings. He also revealed buying company stock at $29 during the COVID sales decline, demonstrating confidence in the company's future pipeline including rare genetic diseases and autoimmune treatments.

items.title: ROSEN, A RANKED AND LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages Bank of America Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BAC
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed securities class action lawsuits against Bank of America Corporation, Lincoln Educational Services Corporation, and Qfin Holdings, Inc. The Bank of America lawsuit alleges systemic weaknesses in its BSA/AML compliance program that failed to properly monitor transactions and file accurate suspicious activity reports, along with sanctions compliance deficiencies. Investors who purchased securities during the specified class periods may be eligible for compensation.

items.title: Amazon Spent More on Data Centers Last Quarter Than AWS Earned in Revenue. Should Investors Worry?
items.summary: Amazon spent $53 billion on capital expenditures in Q2 2026, exceeding AWS's $42 billion quarterly revenue, primarily for AI and cloud infrastructure. Management justifies the aggressive spending citing a $496 billion backlog and strong future demand, though free cash flow will face pressure until new data centers become operational. The company raised its 2026 capex forecast by $20 billion to $220 billion, betting on timing and future revenue growth.

items.title: ROSEN, THE FIRST FILING FIRM, Encourages Webull Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm - BULL
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased Webull Corporation securities between April 26, 2025 and October 6, 2026 of an important December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in a securities class action. The lawsuit alleges that Webull made false statements about its operations, claiming its principal business was U.S.-based when in fact its software development, data pipelines, and core engineering depended on PRC-based personnel and infrastructure subject to Chinese law.
